role: Second, independent decode of the same index bytes. This is not the adapter's decoder and nothing in the emitted facts depends on it: adapter.py reads the wire format directly, because there is no `scip` CLI on this host and the `scip` in Homebrew is an integer-programming solver, a different project with the same name. What this binding buys is that the primary decode is checked by something that was not written here -- the schema's own author's field numbers, compiled by protoc, parsed by a protobuf runtime -- so a mistake in the hand-written reader has somewhere to show up other than in its own output.

proto.why_not_vendored: The descriptor set below is compiled from these exact bytes and is what the cross-check needs at runtime; committing 885 further lines of a third party's schema text would add a second copy to keep in step with the digest above, which is the identity that actually decides anything.

descriptor_set.why_a_descriptor_set: protoc --python_out would emit generated code carrying a hard version check against the protobuf runtime, so the cross-check would fail on a runtime mismatch and read as a decode disagreement. A descriptor set is data: any runtime new enough to build a dynamic message reads it, and it is 6 KB rather than a generated module.

regenerate: shasum -a 256 scip.proto   # must print the proto.sha256 above
shasum -a 256 scip.desc    # protoc's own version changes this; record the new pair here

establishes.note: Two decoders agreeing on these bytes is evidence about these bytes. It is not a proof that the hand-written reader handles a construct this fixture never contained.
